notes.text: Central Bank of Malta Directive No. 16, in force since July 2019, caps loan-to-value at 90% for first-time buyers and primary-residence movers (Category I) and at 75% after phase-in for other purchases, with stressed debt service of no more than 40% of income under a 150 basis point rate shock. Category I loans on property worth below EUR 175,000 are exempt from the LTV and DSTI limits, so the rules bind mainly on investors and higher-value homes rather than on entry-level owner-occupiers. The March 2026 notification confirms that the 40% stressed DSTI for individuals is unchanged.

notes.text: In March 2026 the Central Bank of Malta notified a separate stressed debt service coverage ratio of 1.3 times, equivalent to a stressed DSTI of about 77%, for companies borrowing against residential property including buy-to-let, while the 40% stressed DSTI for individuals is unchanged. Corporate borrowers account for only about 1.36% of residential mortgage lending by value, so the change tidies the framework more than it tightens aggregate credit.

notes.text: Malta had the lowest mortgage pricing in the euro area in February 2026, with an average rate of 1.71% on new loans fixed for up to five years against a euro area average of 3.37%. Rates this far below the euro area norm keep debt service low and sustain buyers' purchasing power through the ECB cycle.

notes.text: The Malta Permanent Residence Programme requires applicants to buy a residential property worth at least EUR 375,000 or rent one for at least EUR 14,000 a year, hold it for at least five years and keep a residence in Malta thereafter, alongside government contributions and capital requirements of EUR 500,000 or more, as amended by Legal Notices in 2024 and 2025. The scheme adds non-EU demand at the upper end of the sale and rental markets.

notes.text: The National Statistics Office compiles Malta's house price index from Tax and Customs Administration records of final notarial deeds for apartments, maisonettes and houses bought by households, using hedonic models by dwelling type. New and existing dwellings cannot be separated, the index covers Malta and Gozo as a whole, and the latest four quarters are provisional because of late contract registrations.
